newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cosmetics firm seeks listing in mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish cosmetics firm seeks listing in mid-1997.

text.p: The Polish cosmetics company Pollena Ewa SA wants to enter the main market of the Warsaw Stock Exchange in mid-1997 after a May share issue, the company board's plenipotentiary said on Wednesday.

Wojciech Jablonski told Reuters that the company planned an extraordinary shareholders meeting in January to decide on the issue and wanted to submit a prospectus to the Securities Commission (KPW) by March 30.
"We plan to enter the bourse, the main market, in the middle of next year....We assume the issue will be in May or June," Jablonski said.
He said Pollena Ewa's earlier plans of entering the bourse at the beginning of the year were revised because the company wanted to pick the best moment for flotation.
Lodz-based Pollena Ewa, owned in 25 percent by state-owned commercial bank Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA, made a net profit of 2.5 million zlotys in 1995 on 42.2 million zlotys in sales.
It expects this year's net to reach 1.7 million zlotys on 46.6 million zlotys in sales.
